articles.title: How is HbA1c calculated? Expert explains what your diabetes test really means
articles.description: HbA1c is a blood test that reflects average blood glucose exposure over the previous two to three months by measuring the percentage of haemoglobin with glucose attached to it; it is not calculated by averaging fasting and post-meal sugar readings. Dr Pranav Ghody explained that HbA1c is a weighted average, with recent blood glucose levels having a greater influence, and can be converted to estimated average glucose using the formula eAG (mg/dL) = 28.7 × HbA1c − 46.7. However, factors such as conditions affecting red blood cell lifespan, haemoglobin variants, recent blood loss or transfusion can affect the result, so HbA1c should sometimes be interpreted alongside glucose readings or other tests. Unlike a glucometer, which shows blood sugar at a particular moment, HbA1c provides a broader picture of glucose levels over several weeks to months.
